instruction: Please create an SSH user named "jack" with password "J@ck#MyP@ss321" on Ubuntu who is only allowed to access the folder "/home/shared1".

result.command: USERNAME="jack"; HOMEDIR="/home/shared1"; PASSWORD="J@ck#MyP@ss321"; ./check_password.sh "$USERNAME" "$PASSWORD" && [ "$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)" = "$HOMEDIR" ] && [ $(stat -c "%A" "$HOMEDIR" | cut -b 3) = "w" ] && echo "Password, home directory, and write permission check passed" || echo "Check failed"

include: Password, home directory, and write permission check passed

metadata.explanation: Task creates SSH user 'jack' with password 'J@ck#MyP@ss321' restricted to folder '/home/shared1'. Evaluator verifies: (1) SSH password authentication works, (2) home directory is set to /home/shared1, (3) user has write permission to the folder.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Incomplete verification - evaluator does NOT verify the core requirement that user is 'only allowed to access' /home/shared1
The instruction requires the user to be RESTRICTED to the folder (chroot jail or similar), but evaluator only checks: (1) password works, (2) home directory is set, (3) write permission exists
Missing verification: Does NOT test if user can actually access other directories outside /home/shared1
A user can have home=/home/shared1 but still freely access /etc, /var, /tmp, etc. The evaluator would incorrectly pass this case
Proper verification would need to: SSH as the user, attempt to navigate outside /home/shared1, verify access is denied, or check SSH config for ChrootDirectory/ForceCommand settings
The evaluator fundamentally cannot verify the security restriction requirement in the instruction
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add test to SSH as 'jack' and attempt to access directories outside /home/shared1 (e.g., 'cd /', 'ls /etc') and verify these commands fail or are blocked
Check SSH daemon config (/etc/ssh/sshd_config) for ChrootDirectory or ForceCommand internal-sftp settings for user 'jack'
Verify that when logged in as 'jack', commands like 'pwd' show / as /home/shared1 (indicating chroot)
Test that 'jack' cannot navigate to parent directories (e.g., 'cd ..' should not escape /home/shared1)
Alternative: If the task only requires setting home directory (not true restriction), then simplify the instruction to remove 'only allowed to access' language
